claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can increase the thermal conductivity of W–Cu composites relative to conventional sintering.
Spark plasma sintering reduces interfacial porosity in W–Cu composites.
Spark plasma sintering improves connectivity between the W and Cu phases.
An SPS-processed W–Cu composite can retain the mechanical durability required for heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications.
An SPS-processed W–Cu composite can retain the irradiation resistance required for fusion-reactor joint applications.
Optimizing SPS temperature, pressure, and dwell time can consolidate tungsten and copper powders effectively.
SPS produces a denser, well-bonded W–Cu interface structure.
SPS refines the microstructure of W–Cu composites.
Rapid heating and high pressure during SPS accelerate consolidation.
Faster SPS consolidation minimizes interfacial defects in W–Cu composites.
Reducing interfacial defects lowers thermal boundary resistance between W and Cu.
Lower thermal boundary resistance improves phonon and electron transport through the composite.
Preserving microstructural integrity maintains mechanical strength.
Preserving microstructural integrity maintains irradiation resistance.
The predicted improvements should persist under high-temperature and irradiation conditions relevant to fusion-reactor joints.
Poorly controlled SPS parameters can cause undesirable grain growth or phase segregation.
Grain growth or phase segregation caused by deviations from optimized SPS parameters may eliminate the predicted benefits.
